proof:
Source: parent proof, step 6 (“The set of orthogonal projections of rank ℓ is compact in the space of linear maps, so there are ℓ-dimensional subspaces π₁,…,π_N such that every ℓ-dimensional π has ‖p_π − p_{π_j}‖ < 1/16 for some j”); Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, chapter-03.txt lines 220–226. We state it for the n-dimensional complements T_j = π_j^⊥: since p_{π^⊥} = I − p_π, ‖p_{π^⊥} − p_{π'^⊥}‖ = ‖p_π − p_{π'}‖ = d(π, π') in Simon's notation (3), so the two formulations are equivalent; the sibling uses ε = 1/16.

1. Let S := {p_Q : Q an n-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P} ⊆ L(ℝ^P), the finite-dimensional normed space of linear maps with the operator norm.
2. Every orthogonal projection has norm ≤ 1 (Mathlib `Submodule.starProjection_norm_le`), so S ⊆ B̄₁(0).
3. L(ℝ^P) is finite-dimensional, hence proper; so B̄₁(0) is compact, hence totally bounded, and so is its subset S.
4. By total boundedness there is a finite set t ⊆ S with S ⊆ ⋃_{L∈t} B_ε(L) (Mathlib `finite_approx_of_totallyBounded`).
5. Every L ∈ t equals p_{T_L} for some n-dimensional subspace T_L (choose one). Enumerate t as L₁,…,L_N and put T_j := T_{L_j}; each T_j is n-dimensional.
6. If Q is n-dimensional then p_Q ∈ S, so ‖p_Q − L_j‖ < ε for some j, i.e. ‖p_Q − p_{T_j}‖ < ε. (If ℝ^P has no n-dimensional subspace, S = t = ∅ and N = 0 works vacuously.) ∎
key_steps: The set S of rank-n orthogonal projections lies in the closed unit ball of the finite-dimensional space L(ℝ^P).
Hence S is totally bounded: finitely many points of S are ε-dense in S.
Write those points as projections p_{T_j} with dim T_j = n.
